findings.issue_text: [BUG] isAccessTokenId's matchesSafely both reads the wrong character range (substring(3,5) instead of substring(4,6)) and inverts the match condition (returns false when the grant shortcut EQUALS the expected value), so the matcher rejects every correctly-encoded token id and accepts ids with the wrong grant. Every test using expectCodeToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken fails on tokens encoded with the expected grant shortcut (e.g. 'trltac:...' expected 'ac': substring(3,5) yields 'ta' which != 'ac', so the equals branch triggers return false), while a token minted under a different grant slips through as a false positive, silently masking cross-grant regressions.

[BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed") twice; the second invocation, labeled 'Null rawTokenId not allowed', never validates rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId passes validation and only surfaces later as an unguarded NPE. A caller constructing AccessTokenContext with a null rawTokenId gets no fail-fast error at construction; encodeTokenId then silently produces a token id ending in ':null' (or a downstream NPE at the ':' concatenation site), corrupting the jti that events and revocation logic key on.

[BUG] postInit registers grant shortcuts without validating that each OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() is exactly 2 characters, while getTokenContextFromTokenId hard-fails (IllegalArgumentException) on any encoded context whose length is not 6. Any custom/deployed grant factory returning a shortcut other than 2 characters (e.g. 'device' or an empty string) produces token ids whose prefix length != 6, so every subsequent getTokenContextFromTokenId call on those tokens throws IllegalArgumentException and token validation/introspection paths that parse the id break at runtime, not at startup where the duplicate-shortcut check lives.

[ADVISORY] The public static nested class Context loses its copy constructor Context(Context) while gaining grantType, so any existing or out-of-tree caller that clones a Context no longer compiles, and no in-diff replacement path sets grantType on a cloned context. Extensions or in-repo callers that previously copied a Context to reuse it (e.g. building a modified request) now must reconstruct it field-by-field; any such caller that survives compilation via reflection or is ported forward will produce a Context whose getGrantType() is null, flowing 'na' into every encoded token id.

[ADVISORY] The duplicate-shortcut validation relies on grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size(), which cannot detect a shortcut equal to another grant's ID (e.g. a shortcut literally 'na' or 'password') because such a collision still yields equal map sizes while overwriting an existing mapping. A future grant factory whose shortcut collides with the reserved UNKNOWN value 'na' or another grant's ID silently overwrites the existing map entry at startup, causing the displaced grant's tokens to decode to the wrong grant type with no error at deploy time.

[BUG] The isAccessTokenId matcher has an off-by-one and an inverted condition: it reads items[0].substring(3, 5) (characters 3-4) instead of substring(4, 6) (characters 4-5) for the grant shortcut, and it returns false when the extracted value EQUALS the expected shortcut. For a correctly encoded id like 'onrtac:uuid', substring(3,5) is 'ta', which never equals 'ac', so the guard `if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is never taken by the intended path — but for ids where chars 3-4 happen to equal the expected shortcut the matcher rejects the correct id, and it accepts any id whose chars 3-4 differ from the expected shortcut, so every expectation either fails or asserts nothing about the real grant shortcut; the updated expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken assertions in this diff verify the wrong bytes.

[BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice and never validates rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId passes validation. A null rawTokenId silently produces an encoded token id ending in ':null' (or just the context prefix via string concat of null), creating tokens whose id cannot be round-tripped through getTokenContextFromTokenId as intended; the second duplicate requireNonNull is dead code that masks the missing check.

[BUG] The Context(Context) copy constructor is deleted, and grantType is only populated from formParams in the primary constructor, so any code path that previously duplicated a Context (or rebuilds one from an existing instance) loses the grantType field with no way to set it (there is no setGrantType). Callers that copied a Context (out-of-tree SPI implementations extending OAuth2GrantType, since Context and its copy constructor are public API in an SPI package) now fail to compile or, if they use the primary constructor with copied formParams, silently re-derive grantType from a formParams map that may not contain grant_type — producing tokens encoded with the 'na' unknown-grant shortcut instead of the real grant.

[ADVISORY] GRANT_TYPE is set in createTokenResponse and in two ad-hoc call sites (PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType, StandardTokenExchangeProvider, TokenManager.validateToken) rather than centrally, so any grant implementation that builds its token response without going through OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse (the same parallel-enumeration problem the shortcut getters solved one factory at a time) yields 'na' context. The next grant type added (or an existing one whose token path bypasses createTokenResponse, e.g. a custom grant SPI) silently encodes tokens with the unknown-grant shortcut; staff-level fix is to derive it in TokenManager/initToken from the active grant context rather than scattering setAttribute calls at four sites in this diff.

[ADVISORY] Duplicate-shortcut validation only compares map sizes, which misses collisions where a grant's shortcut equals the UNKNOWN sentinel 'na' (put into both maps after the loop) or equals another grant's full id — both produce equal-size maps with corrupted/ambiguous mappings. A grant factory registering shortcut 'na' overwrites the UNKNOWN mapping with no error at startup; tokens for that grant and tokens with missing context become indistinguishable in the encoded id, and the corruption is only discovered when decoding returns the wrong grant type.

[ADVISORY] getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut lazily mutate the shared ConcurrentHashMaps at request time with no synchronization between the check and the put, and without re-running the duplicate-shortcut validation. Two concurrent requests resolving an undiscovered grant can both put entries, and a dynamically deployed grant whose shortcut collides with an existing one bypasses the postInit size check entirely, silently overwriting an existing grant's mapping in grantsByShortcuts.

[ADVISORY] initToken's new encoding path (encoder lookup, context construction, encodeTokenId) plus the validateToken GRANT_TYPE attribute have no coverage in this diff beyond the pure unit test DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest, which exercises only encode/decode round-trips on a hand-built factory. A regression in the integration point — e.g. initToken throwing IllegalStateException for a grant whose shortcut is unregistered (encodeTokenId throws for unknown grantType, and only 'na'/refresh/password/client-credentials/token-exchange/pre-authorized paths set the attribute in this diff, so CIBA/device/authorization-code rely on context.getGrantType() being non-null from formParams) — would break all token issuance, and no test in the diff would catch it before the integration suites outside this PR run.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext dereferences clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getUserSession() without a null guard and reads persistence state before the offline check, duplicating the SessionType-vs-persistenceState logic that TokenManager.initToken previously encoded inline (the 'TRANSIENT implies token.subject(user.getId())' branch at TokenManager line ~1056 is now decoupled from the encoder's TRANSIENT classification). The two TRANSIENT definitions can drift: initToken's subject-omission branch keys off userSession.getPersistenceState() directly while the encoder keys off the same enum via a different call chain; a future change to one site (e.g. treating detached sessions differently) desynchronizes the encoded session-type shortcut from actual token behavior, misleading consumers of the encoded context.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId inverts the grant-shortcut check (`if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`) and also reads the wrong character range (the 2-char grant shortcut occupies indices 4-5 of the context prefix, not 3-4). The matcher returns false when the grant shortcut DOES match and falls through to accept UUID when it does not, so every expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken assertion in the test suite passes on the wrong grant type and fails on the right one — the grant-type validation the tests are supposed to enforce is silently negated.

[BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice; the second check intended for rawTokenId checks grantType again, so rawTokenId is never null-checked. A null rawTokenId is accepted and an access token id of the form '<ctx>:null' (or '<ctx>') can be minted, which getTokenContextFromTokenId will later parse as a raw id of the literal string 'null', corrupting token-id correlation in events and introspection.

[ADVISORY] Context.grantType is captured once from formParams at construction time, but setFormParams() can replace the form parameters afterwards without re-reading the grant type, leaving getGrantType() stale or null. Any grant flow that mutates form params after Context construction (or constructs Context with an empty map and sets params later) records grantType=null in clientSessionContext, so the encoded token id gets the 'na' UNKNOWN shortcut even though the request carried a well-known grant type — downstream consumers decoding the id misclassify the token.

[ADVISORY] The new encoded token-id format is wired into initToken unconditionally with no realm option, feature flag, or SPI configuration to revert to plain UUID token ids. Every realm, including those with no interest in token context, immediately starts emitting 'onrtac:<uuid>'-style access token ids; operators whose tooling, SIEM rules, or external integrations assume opaque UUID token ids (and the TOKEN_ID event details asserted across the testsuite) get a breaking format change that cannot be disabled without a code deploy.

[ADVISORY] grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts are package-private mutable ConcurrentHashMaps mutated both by postInit and lazily at request time (getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut), plus directly poked by the unit test, instead of being private with accessors. The lazy-refresh path writes entries after the postInit duplicate-shortcut validation has already run, so a shortcut collision introduced at runtime (or by test manipulation) bypasses the size-based invariant check and silently overwrites an existing grant's mapping, corrupting decode of previously issued token ids.

[ADVISORY] Duplicate-shortcut detection compares only map sizes after inserting both maps plus the fixed 'na' entry, which fails to catch a grant id equal to 'na' or a shortcut colliding with 'na' (both maps still end up equal-sized). A custom grant registered with id or shortcut 'na' passes startup validation but is indistinguishable from the UNKNOWN sentinel when decoding token ids, so tokens from that grant are reported as unknown grant type.

[BUG] The isAccessTokenId matcher has both an off-by-one slice and an inverted equality check: it extracts items[0].substring(3, 5) (characters 4-5) while the grant shortcut occupies indices 4-5 of the 6-char prefix, and it returns false when that substring equals the expected shortcut. Every call to expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken fails its TOKEN_ID assertion even for a correctly encoded token, because the matcher rejects precisely the value it is supposed to accept; the guard can never go green, so either these tests fail or they are not being run (stand-in guard that proves nothing).

[BUG] Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) is duplicated twice and Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId) is never called, so a null rawTokenId passes validation. An AccessTokenContext constructed with a null rawTokenId encodes a token id like 'onrtna:null' (encodeTokenId does plain string concatenation), silently producing a collision-prone literal 'null' id in issued tokens and in event TOKEN_ID details instead of failing fast at construction.

[ADVISORY] The wire format (6-char prefix, three 2-char fields, ':' separator) is hard-coded knowledge duplicated across the decoder substring offsets here and a third independent copy in the test matcher's substring(3,5). The next format change (adding a field, changing shortcut length) requires synchronously updating encoder, decoder, and the test matcher; any missed site silently parses wrong fields — the test matcher already demonstrates exactly this drift happening in this very diff.

[ADVISORY] The lazy 'refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed' paths in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut mutate the grant maps at runtime without the duplicate-shortcut validation enforced in postInit, and grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts are package-private mutable fields. A custom grant deployed at runtime whose shortcut collides with an existing one silently overwrites the first grant's mapping in ConcurrentHashMap (last-writer-wins), decoding tokens to the wrong grant type with no startup error; the test also reaches in and replaces these fields directly, coupling the test to this mutable structure.

[ADVISORY] The public Context(Context) copy constructor is removed from the OAuth2GrantType.Context public nested class without any replacement. Out-of-tree providers or extensions that copy a Context (the only reason such a constructor exists on a public SPI class) fail to compile on upgrade; in-repo call sites are updated but the public surface break is silent for external consumers.

[ADVISORY] The Details.TOKEN_ID event payload format silently changes from a bare UUID to 'XXXXXX:<uuid>' for all token-issuing events, which is a breaking change for external consumers of the event SPI (event listeners, syslog/json event providers, monitoring integrations). Any deployed event listener that stores, joins on, or correlates TOKEN_ID as a UUID breaks or produces unparseable keys after upgrade; only the in-repo test matcher was updated, no versioning or config gate exists for the format change.

[ADVISORY] getShouldUseLightweightToken is widened from package-private instance method to public static solely so DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider can call it. The lightweight-token decision logic becomes part of the public mapper surface and is now coupled into the encoder, so a future change to that decision has a second (non-mapper) caller to keep consistent; a named shared helper/location would avoid the widening.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId() inverts its equality check and uses the wrong substring offset, so the matcher always fails for a correctly-encoded id: it returns false when items[0].substring(3,5) EQUALS the expected shortcut (should return true), and it slices chars 4-5 when the encoder puts the grant shortcut at chars 5-6 (substring(4,6)). Every test using expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken with a correctly formatted 'trrtac:<uuid>'-style id fails to match, breaking the very tests this diff updated; if anyone 'fixes' tests by reordering, the matcher silently validates the wrong thing.

[ADVISORY] The globally visible access-token id (jti) format is changed unconditionally from a UUID to '<6-char-context>:<uuid>' with no realm option, feature flag, or scope limitation, applying the framework to every issued token rather than only where the context encoding is consumed. Any downstream consumer, event indexer, test harness, or integration that assumes token ids are UUIDs (e.g. the original isUUID() assertions, external idp/account tooling, audit pipelines) breaks in behavior without an explicit opt-in, and this cannot be disabled without a code deploy; the decode side (getTokenContextFromTokenId) is only exercised by a unit test in this diff, so production value of the encoded prefix is unproven before it changes all token ids.

[ADVISORY] The public Context(Context) copy constructor on the grant SPI base class was deleted rather than deprecated, silently removing an out-of-tree-callable API surface. Custom grant implementations (or in-tree callers outside this diff) that construct Context from another Context stop compiling on upgrade; the attribute-carrying path is also lost — a copy would not have carried grantType anyway, indicating the constructor was dropped for convenience rather than reviewed as an SPI break.

[BUG] The constructor validates grantType twice (Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) appears twice) and never null-checks rawTokenId despite the intended 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' check. A null rawTokenId passes construction and surfaces later as 'na:null'-style or NPE-prone encoded ids ('...:null' string concat) instead of failing fast at the intended validation point.

[ADVISORY] The lazy 'refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed' caching in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut mutates the shared ConcurrentHashMaps at request time, and the duplicate-shortcut validation is only the size-equality check, which cannot detect two different grants sharing the same shortcut when both are also present as id collisions. First-request races populate maps concurrently (benign but unreviewed), and two third-party grant providers with the same shortcut pass postInit validation only if their ids also collide (both mapping directions collide symmetrically), leaving a silently ambiguous shortcut that decodes tokens to the wrong grant type; the failing-case error message tells the operator to check 'same ID or shortcut' but the check itself does not enforce distinct shortcuts.

[BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice — the second check intended for rawTokenId validates grantType instead, so a null rawTokenId is never rejected and surfaces later as an unguarded NPE (e.g. in encodeTokenId's string concatenation producing a token id of 'onrtna:null'). A null rawTokenId passed by a caller (or custom TokenContextEncoderProvider implementation relying on the documented null-check contract) produces a token id literally containing 'null' instead of failing fast at construction; the contract the constructor promises is not enforced.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId inverts the grant-shortcut check — 'if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;' rejects exactly the tokens it should accept (and the substring indices 3-5 also mismatch the encoder layout, where the grant shortcut occupies chars 4-6 of the prefix). Every expectation built with expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken fails against correctly-encoded token ids (matcher returns false on match), so these suite assertions fail loudly, or after an inevitable 'fix' by removal the grant-type assertion silently accepts any token id.

[ADVISORY] IllegalArgumentException messages interpolate the raw, attacker-supplied encodedTokenId verbatim into exception text, which propagates into server logs and error responses. An attacker can craft token ids containing newlines/CRLF or misleading text that lands unfiltered in Keycloak's logs and admin-facing error output (log-forging / log-injection), polluting audit trails on a security-relevant path (token validation).

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId accepts any colon-less string as a valid token id, returning a context with UNKNOWN types and the raw input as rawTokenId, with no format validation on that path. Whatever consumes getTokenContextFromTokenId downstream (introspection/offline-validation paths built on this framework) receives attacker-controlled rawTokenId content of arbitrary length/content with no syntax gate, inviting each future consumer to re-implement its own validation or pass it unchecked into lookups.

[BUG] The isAccessTokenId matcher's grant-type check is doubly broken: it extracts the wrong character range AND inverts the comparison, so it never enforces the expected grant shortcut. The check `items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` reads characters at indices 3-4 of the 6-char prefix (e.g. "onrtac" -> "ta"), not indices 4-5 where the grant shortcut lives, so it never equals the expected value; additionally `if (... equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects the correct token and accepts a wrong one. Net effect: the matcher only verifies items[1] is a UUID, so expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken pass with ANY grant shortcut (or even a garbage 6-char prefix), giving false confidence that the new token-id encoding encodes the correct grant type.

[BUG] The second null-check validates grantType instead of rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId is accepted by the constructor. `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed")` is duplicated on line 89 where rawTokenId should be checked; a null rawTokenId flows through and later breaks encodeTokenId (producing 'prefix:null' token IDs) instead of failing fast at construction — and the new unit test never exercises a null rawTokenId, so this gap is unverified.

[ADVISORY] The new unit test covers only the decode path via hand-built factory maps; getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext (the production write path that derives SessionType/TokenType/grantType) has zero coverage in this diff. All new branches in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext (TRANSIENT vs offline vs online session detection, lightweight-vs-regular via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken, and the UNKNOWN-grant fallback when Constants.GRANT_TYPE attribute is absent) are untested; a regression there (e.g. always reporting ONLINE, or misreading the lightweight attribute) ships silently while the round-trip tests keep passing. Checked DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java — it only builds AccessTokenContext from hardcoded string IDs and round-trips them; no test constructs a ClientSessionContext.

[ADVISORY] testIncorrectGrantType catches a bare RuntimeException and ignores it, so any unrelated runtime failure (NPE, IllegalStateException from a different defect) satisfies the assertion. If the decoder's exception type or the failure point changes (e.g. an NPE from a factory misconfiguration thrown before the IllegalArgumentException), the test still passes, masking a broken error path; asserting IllegalArgumentException specifically would pin the intended behavior.

[ADVISORY] The test bypasses DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit and hand-populates grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts, so the duplicate-shortcut validation and lazy grant-mapping refresh in the factory are never exercised. The postInit size-mismatch IllegalStateException (the guard against duplicate grant shortcuts across the nine grant factories) and the getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut lazy-refresh paths (lines 105-133 of DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory) have no test; a regression that breaks duplicate-shortcut detection or the rolling-deploy lazy-mapping path would pass CI, and the test setup also silently diverges from the real map construction (which adds the 'na' entry in postInit, not via a hand-built map).

[BUG] isAccessTokenId extracts the grant shortcut with substring(3,5), but the encoded format puts the grant shortcut at indices 4-5 (2 chars sessionType + 2 chars tokenType), so it compares 'tt[1]+gt[0]' against the expected shortcut and always mismatches. Every consumer of expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken fails its assertion (e.g. 'onrtrt:uuid' yields substring(3,5)='tr' vs expected 'rt'), turning these test helpers into guaranteed-failure matchers.

[BUG] The constructor checks requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") twice and never null-checks rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId is accepted despite the message claiming it is rejected. A null rawTokenId silently produces an encoded token id like 'onrtna:null-terminated...' with a 'null' raw id component instead of failing fast, propagating an invalid token identifier into issued tokens.

[ADVISORY] The token-ID format is being migrated from bare UUIDs to 'context:uuid' with no backward/forward compatibility strategy for the rolling-deploy window: tokens minted by new nodes carry a 7-char prefixed id that pre-upgrade nodes have never seen. During a rolling upgrade, old nodes receiving new-format token ids (revocation, introspection, any server-side lookup keyed on the token id) treat them as opaque/foreign identifiers, causing token validation/lookup failures until all nodes are upgraded; this is a one-way format change with no documented fallback or dual-format handling.

[ADVISORY] The duplicate-shortcut validation can silently miss collisions: if a grant provider's id or shortcut collides with the reserved 'na' (UNKNOWN), the later ConcurrentHashMap.put overwrites the entry and the size-equality check still passes. A custom grant whose id/shortcut is 'na' (or collides with a built-in shortcut after the overwrite) gets one of its two mappings dropped without any error, so tokens encoded with that grant later fail decode with 'Unknown value for grant type'.

[ADVISORY] grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts are package-private mutable fields assigned only in postInit and lazily mutated from getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut on request threads, with no synchronization guard against concurrent re-registration during the lazy refresh path. Two concurrent requests hitting an unregistered grant type both run the lazy-mapping block; ConcurrentHashMap makes individual puts safe, but any caller touching these fields before postInit (as the test does via direct field writes) or a factory reused across re-inits sees NPE or stale maps, and the mutable package-private state makes the next provider change riskier.

[BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType) twice and never validates rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId passes construction and surfaces later as an NPE at token-encoding time instead of a clear startup/validation error. A caller that constructs AccessTokenContext with a null rawTokenId gets the null deep into encodeTokenId (string concatenation yields '...onrtac:null' or NPE in downstream consumers), corrupting token IDs rather than failing fast at the guarded boundary the constructor pretends to provide.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId extracts the grant shortcut with items[0].substring(3, 5), which is the last char of the tokenType shortcut plus the first char of the grant shortcut (the grant shortcut occupies chars 4-5, i.e. substring(4,6)), and additionally returns false when that substring equals the expected shortcut, inverting the check. For a correct id like 'trl tcc' the extracted substring 'tc' never equals 'cc', so the equality branch never triggers and the matcher falls through to the UUID check — every expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken assertion silently accepts any grant shortcut, making the new grant-encoding verification vacuous across the whole test suite; had the substring logic been 'fixed' to land on the right chars, the inverted return would then reject every correct token.

[ADVISORY] The public Context(Context) copy constructor is deleted with no replacement, removing part of the Context public surface. Out-of-tree grant-type implementations or customizations that clone the grant Context (the constructor existed precisely to allow copying) fail to compile against this version, and the diff provides no migration path or deprecation period for that caller.

[ADVISORY] grantType is captured once in the Context constructor from formParams.getFirst(GRANT_TYPE), but setFormParams can replace the form parameters afterwards without re-deriving grantType, so the cached value goes stale. Any code path that swaps formParams after Context construction (the very existence of setFormParams shows this is an anticipated flow) encodes the wrong grant shortcut into issued token IDs, permanently baking a misattributed grant type into the token identifier with no runtime error to surface the discrepancy.

[ADVISORY] The newly-required OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() has no default implementation, and postInit puts factory results into ConcurrentHashMaps where a null shortcut or null id throws NPE. Third-party grant providers compiled against the previous interface either fail to load (abstract-method mismatch) or, if they return null from getShortcut, crash server startup with an NPE inside ConcurrentHashMap.put — a new hard startup failure introduced by this diff rather than a per-grant degradation.

[ADVISORY] The duplicate-shortcut validation compares grantsByShortcuts.size() against grantsToShortcuts.size(), which can coincide (same-ID + same-shortcut duplicates collapse both maps equally) and the 'na' sentinel put happens after the check, so collisions can slip through or be masked. Two grant providers sharing both id and shortcut, or a future grant whose shortcut is 'na', register silently: tokens issued by one grant decode as the other grant, with the encoder reporting the wrong grant type as if it were authoritative.
